questions.question: What were the main issues involved in the Second Great Debate in IR?
questions.solution_html:
• Second Great Debate in International Relations-centred on the methodological dispute
  • between Traditionalism and Behaviouralism- traditionalists emphasised historical analysis
  • philosophy and political judgement- scholars like Hans Morgenthau and others favoured
  • case studies and historical insight- treated international relations as a subjective social science
  • rooted in human judgment, norms and context- behaviouralists advocated scientific methods
  • empirical observation, quantification and systematic theory- shifts analytical vocabulary from
  • abstract "decisions" or "intentions" to measurable actions, stimuli, and response patterns
  • building to study international politics- borrowed methods and concepts from psychology
  • sociology, and cybernetics-example-Morton Kaplan’s systems theory.
questions.final_answer: sociology, and cybernetics-example-Morton Kaplan’s systems theory
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the difference between positivist and post-positivist ontological / assumptions.
questions.solution_html:
• Positivism assumes an objective reality- international politics can be studied through
  • observation, causal explanation and scientific methods- post-positivism questions the
  • neutrality of knowledge- emphasises interpretation, discourse, historical context and power
  • ontologically, positivists generally accept an independently existing reality- post-positivists
  • examine how social realities are constructed and understood
questions.final_answer: examine how social realities are constructed and understood
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: How does Liberalism explain the possibility of cooperation among states?
questions.solution_html:
• Liberalism explains international cooperation through economic interdependence
  • international institutions, democracy and shared interests- Institutions reduce uncertainty
  • facilitate information-sharing- monitor agreements- democratic governments face domestic
  • accountability- trade increases the costs of conflict- these mechanisms encourage states to
  • pursue mutual gains and resolve disputes through negotiation.
questions.final_answer: pursue mutual gains and resolve disputes through negotiation
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Analyze the mechanics of "Functional Spillover" using a concrete historical or / theoretical example.
questions.solution_html:
• Functional spillover occurs when cooperation in one policy area creates pressure for
  • integration in related areas- European integration illustrates this process- cooperation in coal
  • and steel encouraged collaboration in trade, markets, and other economic policies- Functional
  • interdependence generates new demands- encourage institutions and political actors to
  • expand regional integration.
questions.final_answer: expand regional integration
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: How can Game Theory be applied to explain strategic decision-making between / two competing states?
questions.solution_html:
• Game theory explains strategic decisions- modelling states as actors whose outcomes
  • depend on one another’s choices-Prisoner’s Dilemma- shows why two rational individuals
  • might not cooperate, even when it is in their best interest to do so- two competing states may
  • increase military spending despite mutual losses- each fears vulnerability if the other arms
  • repeated interaction, communication and credible agreements can encourage cooperation.
questions.final_answer: repeated interaction, communication and credible agreements can encourage cooperation
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Using Realist assumptions, how would you explain a state's decision to form a / strategic alliance with another state?
questions.solution_html:
• Realism explains strategic alliances as instruments for protecting national interests and
  • enhancing security- states assess threats- capabilities- geography- the distribution of power
  • before partnering-through balancing, weaker states may unite against a stronger rival
  • alliances remain conditional- because changing threats and interests can undermine
  • commitments.
questions.final_answer: commitments
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the relationship between "power" and "knowledge" in Postmodern IR / theory.
questions.solution_html:
• Postmodern IR theory- argues that power and knowledge are mutually constitutive
  • dominant institutions and discourses shape what counts as legitimate knowledge- knowledge
  • categorises populations and legitimises political authority- drawing on Michel Foucault
  • postmodernists examine how security narratives, geopolitical representations, and expert
  • claims reproduce hierarchies and influence international practices-R B J Walker, Richard
  • Ashley, James Der Derian, David Campbell- critiqued state sovereignty, the
  • domestic/international dichotomy and the concept of anarchy-challenged traditional theories
  • like realism and liberalism by rejecting objective truth, universal metanarratives, and state
  • centric assumptions-.
questions.final_answer: centric assumptions
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: How does Constructivism differentiate the characteristics of Hobbesian and / Lockean conceptions of Anarchy?
questions.solution_html:
• Constructivism distinguishes Hobbesian and Lockean anarchy through socially
  • constructed state identities and norms- Hobbesian anarchy treats rivals as enemies- making
  • violence and survival central- Lockean anarchy treats states as competitors- recognise one
  • another’s sovereignty- consequently, states may compete without seeking each other’s
  • destruction or denying territorial independence.
questions.final_answer: destruction or denying territorial independence
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: According to Gilpin’s framework, in what specific ways does the state’s pursuit / of power shape the international market?
questions.solution_html:
• Robert Gilpin’s political economy framework- explains how state power shapes
  • international markets- through trade policies- monetary arrangements- investment rules
  • economic institutions- powerful states establish rules favouring their interests- protect
  • strategic industries- influence access to markets- changes in relative power can produce
  • demands to revise existing economic arrangements and institutions.
questions.final_answer: demands to revise existing economic arrangements and institutions
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Why is the semi-periphery considered essential for the political stability of the / modern world-economy?
questions.solution_html:
• Immanuel Wallerstein’s world-systems theory- semi-periphery occupies an intermediate
  • position between core and periphery- combines industrial development with continuing
  • economic dependence- absorbs pressures from both groups- provides opportunities for
  • upward mobility- intermediate position moderates polarisation- reduces systemic tension
  • contributes to the relative stability of the capitalist world-economy.
questions.final_answer: contributes to the relative stability of the capitalist world-economy
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the major features of the 'First Great Debate' between Idealism and / Realism.
questions.solution_html:
• First Great Debate in International Relations- centred on Idealism and Realism- the
  • theoretical clash between idealism (liberalism) and realism that unfolded during the 1930s
  • and 1940s- Idealism/utopianism-inspired by the aftermath of World War I and Woodrow
  • Wilson’s Fourteen Points- Norman Angell , Leonard Woolf- believed human beings and states
  • are capable of moral progress and cooperative behaviour- Idealists emphasised international
  • law- collective security- diplomacy and institutions to prevent war- Realists criticised these
  • approaches - championed by scholars like E.H. Carr in his 1939 book The Twenty Years' Crisi
  • .argued that power, national interest and human nature fundamentally shape international
  • politics- morality or goodwill does not dictate state actions-debate highlighted competing
  • understandings of peace, conflict and state behaviour.
questions.final_answer: understandings of peace, conflict and state behaviour
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain how Diplomacy acts as a cultural anchor for international society.
questions.solution_html:
• Part of English School of IR- notably developed and advanced by Hedley Bull-- viewed
  • diplomacy as a fundamental institution that helps maintain order in an anarchical society of
  • states-diplomacy acts as a cultural anchor for international society- Martin Wight- diplomacy
  • as the "master-institution" of international relations- facilitate communication, negotiation
  • and peaceful coexistence among culturally diverse states- diplomatic practices establish
  • shared protocols- mutual recognition- conventions of respect- accommodating differences in
  • language, religion and political traditions- diplomacy sustains international norms- reduces
  • misunderstandings- promotes cooperation without eliminating cultural diversity.
questions.final_answer: misunderstandings- promotes cooperation without eliminating cultural diversity
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: “Critical Theory seeks not merely to explain the existing international order but / to transform it.” Evaluate this statement.
questions.solution_html:
• Critical Theory challenges the assumption that international order is natural or inevitable
  • influenced by the Frankfurt School- Robert Cox argued that theory is always for someone and
  • for some purpose- traditional "problem-solving" theories serve the status quo and help elites
  • maintain power- critical theory seeks emancipation- global politics is shaped by deep
  • economic and social structures, history, and human agency rather than fixed, ahistorical laws
  • like "anarchy"-Critical Theory examines domination- inequality- ideological structures while
  • imagining emancipatory alternatives- transforming global institutions remains difficult
  • because entrenched power relations constrain meaningful change.
questions.final_answer: because entrenched power relations constrain meaningful change
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the meaning and major features of Time-Space Compression according / to David Harvey.
questions.solution_html:
• David Harvey’s concept of time-space compression- follows Marx’s concept of
  • annihilation of space by time- describe how capitalism perpetually tries to overcome
  • geographic distance-technological innovation- faster communication- accelerated
  • transportation- reduced the perceived significance of geographical distance and time
  • capitalism drives this process through rapid circulation of commodities, information and
  • finance- global connectivity increases- its benefits remain unequal- intensifying economic
  • competition- cultural transformation and geographical disparities.
questions.final_answer: competition- cultural transformation and geographical disparities
